text: Flight 14 is the first attempt to put a Starship into orbit. Booster 21 and Ship 41 are both third-generation Block 3 vehicles, powered by Raptor 3.
Super Heavy and Starship together hold several thousand tonnes of super-chilled liquid methane and liquid oxygen.
The water deluge comes on to absorb heat and sound from 33 Raptors.
IGNITION
LIFTOFF of Starship!
33 Raptor 3 engines, each rated at about 280 tonnes-force, give Super Heavy more than 9,000 tonnes of thrust at liftoff. They gimbal and throttle to steer the ascent.
Max Q: the most aerodynamic stress the vehicle will see on ascent.
An engine shut down early on Super Heavy. The remaining Raptors keep the ascent on track.
Hot staging! Starship lights its six engines while still attached and pushes off through the vented ring.
Boostback: 31 of the 33 planned engines relight. The burn is designed to run the main LOX tank dry to probe the booster's margins.
Landing burn: 11 of 13 engines light, then the booster steps down to 5, then 3, for a soft splashdown in the Gulf.
A pretty soft splashdown for Super Heavy.

text: The insertion burn uses a single sea-level Raptor fed from the header tanks, a first. It raises perigee out of the atmosphere.
Starship is orbital.
The PEZ dispenser door opens. Satellites slide out one by one. Three of them carry cameras to photograph the ship's heat shield.
Just this one flight was like 20 Falcon 9 flights in terms of bandwidth.

text: All 26 Starlink V3 satellites are deployed: about 26 Tbps of new capacity.
SpaceX will deorbit early, after about one and a half orbits, targeting the northern Pacific contingency zone.
Live HD video from orbit, streamed through Starlink laser links. Another first.
First-ever Starship deorbit burn. One sea-level Raptor lowers perigee into the atmosphere.
We'll hit entry around the 2 hour 47 minute mark, with splashdown about 21 minutes after that.

text: Entry: plasma builds around the heat shield, which includes reflown tiles from Ship 40 and new curved tiles.
Now subsonic, Starship falls belly-first, steering with its four flaps.
Landing flip and landing burn: all three sea-level Raptors relight.
Starship has landed.
